sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Deficit Reverse Lunge is an advanced lunge variation performed from an elevated surface such as a plyometric step, while holding dumbbells for added resistance.

The elevated starting position increases the range of motion, forcing the working leg to travel through a deeper stretch at the bottom of the movement.

This greater range of motion leads to increased glute and quad activation compared to a standard reverse lunge, making it an excellent exercise for building lower body strength and muscle.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Increased range of motion compared to standard reverse lunges
- Greater glute and quad activation from the deeper stretch
- Builds unilateral leg strength and corrects muscle imbalances
- Improves hip mobility and flexibility
- Less knee stress than forward lunge variations
- Enhances balance, coordination, and stability
- Easily scalable by adjusting step height and dumbbell weight

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Quadriceps, Glutes, Hamstrings

Secondary: Calves, Core (Rectus Abdominis, Obliques), Hip Flexors, Adductors, Forearms (grip)

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Stand on top of a plyometric step or elevated platform.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging at your sides.
3. Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core engaged.
4. Feet should be hip-width apart on the platform.
5. Eyes looking straight ahead with a neutral spine.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Step one foot back off the platform, landing on the ball of your foot on the floor behind you.
2. Keep your front knee directly over your ankle as you descend.
3. Lower your back knee towards the ground, keeping your front knee bent at a 90-degree angle.
4. Allow your hip to drop below the level of the platform for a deep stretch.
5. Push through your front foot to return to the starting position on the platform.
6. Repeat on the other side for the desired number of reps.
7. Alternate legs with each rep or complete all reps on one side before switching.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Stepping back too far or not far enough off the platform
- Front knee caving inward during the descent
- Leaning the torso too far forward
- Not utilising the full range of motion the deficit provides
- Losing balance due to an unstable platform
- Rushing through reps and losing control
- Not keeping the front shin relatively vertical

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Plyometric Step or Sturdy Elevated Platform (10-20 cm height)
- Pair of Dumbbells (appropriate weight for your level)
- Flat, Non-Slip Surface
- Optional: Mirror for form checking

sections.heading: Platform Selection
sections.content:
1. Start with a low platform (10-15 cm) and progress to higher as you build strength.
2. Ensure the platform is sturdy and does not wobble.
3. The surface should be non-slip to prevent your foot from sliding.
4. A standard aerobic step or bumper plate works well.
5. The higher the platform, the greater the range of motion and difficulty.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Feet: Hip-width apart, centred on the platform.
2. Grip: Dumbbells held at sides with a neutral grip.
3. Torso: Upright with chest proud and shoulders back.
4. Core: Braced throughout the movement.
5. Head: Neutral, eyes forward.
6. Step Length: Long enough that both knees reach 90 degrees at the bottom.
7. Ensure adequate space behind the platform for the step back.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Reverse Lunge: Standard flat-ground version with less range of motion
- Bulgarian Split Squat: Rear foot elevated for single-leg focus
- Walking Lunge: Continuous stepping lunges for distance
- Step-Up: Single-leg movement onto an elevated surface
- Goblet Squat: Front-loaded squat for quad emphasis
- Forward Lunge: Step forward instead of backward

sections.heading: Deficit Lunge Variations
sections.content:
Deficit Reverse Lunge with Dumbbells: Standard deficit lunge with dumbbells at sides
Deficit Reverse Lunge with Barbell: Barbell across upper back for heavier loading
Deficit Forward Lunge: Step forward off the platform for a different challenge
Deficit Curtsy Lunge: Step back and across for glute medius emphasis
Bodyweight Deficit Reverse Lunge: No added weight for learning the movement
Deficit Reverse Lunge with Pulse: Add pulses at the bottom for time under tension

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Knee Pain: Reduce platform height or switch to flat-ground reverse lunges
Balance Issues: Start with bodyweight only and hold a wall for support
Hip Tightness: Warm up with hip flexor stretches before lunging
Ankle Mobility: Use a lower platform and ensure proper footwear
No Platform: Perform standard reverse lunges from the floor
Lower Back Pain: Keep torso more upright and reduce dumbbell weight
